usual_baseline: Prophylaxis is almost always given. Duration and choice fail. Full compliance ranged 23.7% [2292] to 74.1% [1333]. Correct agent 43.5–65.4% [2292, 1693]. Duration too long in 21–25% [2051, 2292]. Postprocedural doses were appropriate in 48.3% [1577]. Post-incision dosing ran 18.9% [2421] and 26% in appendicectomy [1580].
fix_that_works: Changes built into theatre routine work. Posters and stickers: correct MRSA-unknown agent 18% to 94% [1529]. A new protocol with posters: courses cut to 24 hours, stay 3.33 to 2.04 days, no SSI [1593]. Sign-in/time-out edits and a duration sticker: mean duration 70.4 to 28.2 hours, correct agent 43.5% to 65.3% [2421].
fix_that_fails: MRSA eradication stickers: 1% to only 8% [1529]. Presenting at governance: appropriate prophylaxis 78% to 83%, with more incomplete courses [1255]. Full compliance stayed at 39.8% after a year of QI [2421]. Administration time stayed poorly documented [2863].
consultant_advice: Don't audit whether prophylaxis was given; it nearly always is. Audit duration after surgery and choice of agent, and add a prompt to the WHO time-out or drug chart. Recording SSI and dosing errors, as one large audit did [1333], adds more value.
